title: Motion
subject: Physics

English.simple_explanation: Motion means an object's position changes over time. We describe motion using distance, speed, and time.
English.detailed_explanation: An object is in motion when its position changes compared with a fixed reference point. Average speed is the distance travelled divided by the time taken: speed = distance / time. Real journeys rarely happen at one constant speed the whole way.
English.everyday_example: Walking to a well or shop, cycling to school, or a bus travelling between villages are all examples of motion that can be measured with distance, speed, and time.

local_example.text: Many students walk to school, a shop, a field, or a water source every day. That daily walk is a real, measurable example of motion.
local_example.appropriate_usage: Use as a general local-context draft only until reviewed by a community or content reviewer; do not present it as a claim about any specific student, family, or route.

common_misconceptions: A faster average speed always means the object moved at that exact speed the whole time.
The distance and total time alone tell you everything about a journey, without needing to think about rest stops or a changing pace.
think_question: If two people walk the same distance but one is carrying a heavy load, would you expect their time to be the same? Why or why not?

reasoning_guide.correct_feedback: Good reasoning: you connected carrying a load to a change in walking speed, and therefore a change in time.
reasoning_guide.partial_feedback: You are close. Explain how carrying a load might change walking speed, and how that affects the time taken.
reasoning_guide.misconception_feedback: A heavier load usually changes walking speed for the same distance. Think about how that affects the time taken.

challenge.question: Estimate how long it would take to walk 300 m at a normal walking pace, then explain your estimate.
challenge.hint: An average walking speed is roughly 1 to 1.5 metres per second.
progressive_hints: An average walking speed is roughly 1 to 1.5 metres per second.
Use time = distance / speed with your estimated speed.
Try 300 divided by 1.2 as one reasonable estimate.
challenge.solution: Using a typical walking speed of about 1.2 m/s, 300 m would take roughly 250 seconds (about 4 minutes). Real answers vary with pace, terrain, and load.

quiz_questions.question: Which formula correctly relates speed, distance, and time?
quiz_questions.explanation: Average speed is the distance travelled divided by the time taken, so speed = distance / time.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about how far you go divided by how long it takes.
progressive_hints: Think about how far you go divided by how long it takes.
Speed increases when distance increases or when time decreases.
